rule.description: Reports a function when it compares raw target strings against known architecture vocabulary tokens while also handling the container-platform types, instead of delegating the target-to-platform conversion to the repository's platform mapping API in src/docker/image.rs.

checks.description: Detect functions that re-derive which container platform (architecture/OS pairing) a Rust target implies by comparing raw target string components against a hardcoded architecture vocabulary, while also constructing or handling the container-platform types, instead of asking the repository's platform mapping API (src/docker/image.rs) to perform the target-to-platform conversion.
checks.detected_relation: business function -> locally re-implemented target-to-platform mapping that duplicates the platform mapping API
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The knowledge of how a target triple maps to a container platform is scattered across several call sites; any change to that mapping (new architecture, corrected vocabulary) requires editing every site instead of the one place that owns the conversion.

matches.evidence: custom() splits the rustc host string into components and matches them against hardcoded architecture tokens ("x86_64", "aarch64", "armv7", ...) plus per-component OS words, assembling container platform values (Architecture, Os, ImagePlatform structs) locally and falling back to ImagePlatform::from_target only when its own decoding fails.

with_picked() unpacks the picked target triple by splitting on '-' and matching the components against architecture and OS tokens, then constructs ImagePlatform values inline with hardcoded variant and OS pairings rather than delegating the triple-to-platform conversion to the mapping API.

parse() decodes the toolchain's host triple itself: it derives a linux-host boolean from the trailing triple components and matches the architecture component against tokens such as "powerpc64", "riscv64gc" and "loongarch64" to construct ImagePlatform values locally.

get_possible_image() re-derives the container platform for each candidate target string from a config table: it strips the triple into components, matches the architecture component against hardcoded tokens and pairs it with a locally decoded OS to build ImagePlatform values inline.

engine_info() converts the strings reported by the container engine by matching them against hardcoded OS words and architecture tokens ("linux", "windows", "darwin", "x86_64", "aarch64", ...) to produce ContainerOs and Architecture values locally instead of only asking the platform API's constructors.

run() matches the toolchain host triple's leading component against hardcoded architecture tokens ("x86_64", "aarch64", "s390x", "loongarch64", ...) to derive the host Architecture itself instead of comparing against the platform value the toolchain already exposes.

excluded.reason: The platform mapping API itself (Architecture::new, Os::from_target, ImagePlatform::from_target and their serde conversions) owns the target-to-platform vocabulary; the rule keeps the return-type exemption so any function that genuinely performs the conversion is never reported, which makes the rule repair-agnostic.

Toolchain string parsing that only splits a triple into channel/date/host components without touching container-platform types stays outside the rule: the smell is defined by simultaneously re-deriving vocabulary and handling the platform types.
